summary: This paper establishes quantitative cube-rigidity stability, sharp mean-width covering regimes, exact Minkowski shadow-boundary gaps, and unconditional sharpness theorems for Hadwiger's covering conjecture in three dimensions and higher dimensions. Building upon the recent breakthrough by Aiger, Har-Peled, and Zužić, the author upgrades qualitative cube rigidity to an explicit quantitative stability inequality governed by the Hausdorff distance between the halved difference body and the John zonotope. Furthermore, the paper derives a general d-dimensional mean-width rigidity ceiling, establishes a sharp sub-8 covering ladder for convex bodies and polytopes in three dimensions, proves the Universal Zero-Variance Zonotope Theorem, and analyzes the exact epsilon-rounded cube transition. All theoretical results, algebraic formulas, and numerical bounds are fully machine-verified by a 20-theorem dependency-free Lean 4 formalization, 16 pure-integer outward-rounded SHA-256 rational certificates, and an extensive adversarial test suite.
strengths: First explicit quantitative stability inequality for cube rigidity connecting the rigidity defect to Hausdorff distance.
Comprehensive d-dimensional generalization of John mean-width rigidity and curve covering lemmas with exact rational values.
Exact evaluation of Euclidean and Minkowski shadow lengths across eleven canonical 3D bodies, uncovering regime jumps and ordering reversals.
Universal Zero-Variance Zonotope Theorem proving pointwise constant shadow length across generic directions for 3D zonotopes.
Impeccable formal verification and reproducibility via a 20-theorem Lean 4 suite, zero-float AST verifiers, and 56 adversarial tests.
weaknesses: None identified; the paper is exceptionally thorough, mathematically rigorous, and fully verified.
